overall: A technically solid preliminary mission design with well-justified orbital mechanics and STK access simulations. Key presentation weaknesses include unnumbered figure and table captions, an incomplete sentence in the EOL section, and citing Wikipedia against explicit task instructions.

feedback.summary: You delivered a technically robust preliminary space mission design for Australia, featuring clear justifications for your single-spacecraft architecture, orbital parameters, and ground access simulations. Your technical logic and orbital mechanics analysis are accomplished. To reach professional engineering standards, ensure complete editorial review to eliminate broken text, formally number and caption all figures and tables, and replace non-academic sources such as Wikipedia with authoritative primary literature.
next_steps: Implement standard, numbered captions (e.g., 'Figure 1: STK 3D orbit view') and cross-reference them directly within the body text.
Replace Wikipedia citations with primary technical documentation, such as launch vehicle user manuals or peer-reviewed literature.
Proofread all narrative sections carefully to resolve incomplete sentences, broken formatting lines, and missing orbital parameters like Epoch.

criteria.C2: Your technical design is accomplished, featuring rigorous orbital mechanics calculations for a sun-synchronous orbit, sound trade-offs, and STK ground access simulations. To improve, ensure you specify the epoch for your orbital elements.
criteria.C3: You reached an accomplished conclusion, delivering an effective summary that synthesised your findings across launch, orbital design, ground architecture, and national environmental impact.
criteria.C4: To reach the Accomplished level, ensure figures and tables have numbered, consistent captions rather than plain text labels, remove broken sentences in the EOL section, and avoid prohibited sources like Wikipedia.
